claims.text: Short AIMD trajectories can provide vibrational covariance matrices that retain vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling.
A force-constant model parameterized from those covariance matrices can represent both solid and liquid phases.
A machine-learning potential trained in this two-stage workflow can rapidly sample both solid and liquid configuration spaces.
The hybrid method can yield accurate fusion free energies for multicomponent high-entropy systems at a fraction of the cost of explicit AIMD or TOR-TILD.
Vibrational covariance is a sufficient mediator for encapsulating the entropy contributions and anharmonic interactions relevant to phase free energies.
The covariance-derived information can be embedded into an ML surrogate while preserving the relevant physics.
A Gaussian covariance approximation captures vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling.
Combining the Gaussian approximation with an ML potential approximates complete solid and liquid phase free energies without extended AIMD trajectories.
The hybrid workflow preserves the fidelity of the relevant entropy terms while substantially reducing computational expense in multicomponent systems.
For elemental and binary systems, the hybrid method will have fidelity comparable to explicit AIMD and TOR-TILD.
For high-entropy alloys, the hybrid method will provide an order-of-magnitude speedup.
The method can predict derived fusion observables including melting point and latent heat.
Explicit AIMD free-energy methods and TOR-TILD are highly accurate for elemental and binary systems.
Explicit AIMD and TOR-TILD become prohibitively slow for complex multicomponent alloys.
The Gaussian approximation is most appropriate when atomic displacements are small or moderate.
A covariance-based Gaussian method is applicable in principle to complex crystalline and noncrystalline solids, including high-entropy alloys.
The proposed hybrid method is applicable from binary alloys through high-entropy alloys with five or more principal elements under near-melting conditions.
Prior elemental and binary benchmarks of the proposed approach are promising.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and mechanism state that the covariance/ML workflow retains or preserves electron–vibration coupling and anharmonic effects, whereas the uncertainty field says faithful reproduction of those effects by the ML surrogate remains unvalidated.

The validity boundary requires moderate atomic displacements for a Gaussian approximation, but the proposed scope includes the liquid near melting without explaining how liquid configurations satisfy that restriction.
